dedupe_keys.name: flwbarp benchmark facility location waste bin allocation and routing instances for underground container systems

description: This benchmark supports research on replacing door-to-door waste collection with underground containers at central sites. It was deposited on Mendeley Data by Sina Gläser in February 2021. The underlying planning problem, named the facility location and waste bin allocation and routing problem (FLWBARP), combines six decisions: which sites to open, which customers to assign to each site, how often and on which days of the planning horizon to empty each site, how many containers of which type to install, and which vehicle routes to run, all to minimise total cost. The instances extend the ten instances of the waste bin allocation and routing problem by Hemmelmayr and colleagues (2014), which were themselves built from the periodic routing instances of Cordeau and colleagues (1997) and Crevier and colleagues (2007). The files are free to download online under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the instances are synthetic, derived from classic routing benchmarks, not a real city, and the metadata do not list file formats. Simulation uses: test cases for optimisation of waste collection networks and container siting. Related records: the capacitated waste collection routing data (data-capacitated-waste-collection-routing-p02999) and the Bahía Blanca instances (data-bahia-blanca-waste-collection-routing-instances) are other routing benchmarks, the latter from a real city.
